en: Itivuttaka 93 Tikanipāta, Pañcamavagga Thus it was said. This is the third discourse in the fifth chapter of the Section of Threes. “Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a stone pillar, the person who is like a tree stump, and the person who is like a lotus flower. And how, monks, is one a person like a stone pillar? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hatred toward his mother, his father, his brothers, his sisters, his friends, his companions, his relatives, and his kin; he dwells with a mind full of hatred toward ascetics and brahmins, and even toward the multitude of beings. Just as a stone pillar is not moved by the wind from the east, the west, the north, or the south, so too, monks, this person is not moved by gain or loss, fame or disrepute, praise or blame, pleasure or pain. Thus, monks, is one a person like a stone pillar. And how, monks, is one a person like a tree stump? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hatred toward his mother... [as above] ...toward the multitude of beings. He does not speak words that are true and beneficial, nor does he refrain from speaking words that are false and harmful. Just as a tree stump is not moved by the wind from the east, the west, the north, or the south, so too, monks, this person is not moved by gain or loss, fame or disrepute, praise or blame, pleasure or pain. Thus, monks, is one a person like a tree stump. And how, monks, is one a person like a lotus flower? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind free from hatred toward his mother, his father, his brothers, his sisters, his friends, his companions, his relatives, and his kin; he dwells with a mind free from hatred toward ascetics and brahmins, and even toward the multitude of beings. Just as a lotus flower, though born in the water and grown in the water, rises up above the water and stands unsoiled by the water, so too, monks, this person dwells with a mind free from hatred toward his mother... [as above] ...toward the multitude of beings. He speaks words that are true and beneficial, and he refrains from speaking words that are false and harmful. Thus, monks, is one a person like a lotus flower. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, a certain monk addressed the monks: “Friends, the Blessed One has risen from his seat and gone to his dwelling after saying: ‘Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world... When this was said, another monk spoke thus to that monk: “Friend, do not say that the Blessed One spoke thus. Friend, the Blessed One would never say such a thing. For the Blessed One, friend, would praise the person like a lotus flower, and would censure the person like a stone pillar and the person like a tree stump. Then that monk, having approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him and sat down at one side. Sitting there, he reported to the Blessed One exactly what had occurred. “Monk, that monk did not speak thus out of malice. Monk, that monk spoke the truth. For I, monk, have praised the person like a lotus flower, and I have censured the person like a stone pillar and the person like a tree stump. And why, monk, have I praised the person like a lotus flower? Because, monk, that person is freed from the four floods. Therefore, monk, I have praised the person like a lotus flower. And why, monk, have I censured the person like a stone pillar? Because, monk, that person is bound by the four bonds. Therefore, monk, I have censured the person like a stone pillar. And why, monk, have I censured the person like a tree stump? Because, monk, that person is bound by the four ties. Therefore, monk, I have censured the person like a tree stump. Therefore, monk, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will be like the person like a lotus flower, and we will not be like the person like a stone pillar or the person like a tree stump. Thus, monk, should you train yourselves. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and went to his dwelling. The Fire Sutta.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three fires."
“What are the three?
The fire of lust, the fire of hatred, and the fire of delusion—
these, monks, are the three fires.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“The fire of passion burns mortals;”
Those who are stained and infatuated with sensual pleasures,
and those men who, possessed by the fire of hatred,
take the lives of living beings.
But those who are overcome by delusion, utterly bewildered,
and unskilled in the noble Dhamma— these,
not knowing these fires, [are consumed].
People delight in personal existence;
they increase the realms of hell and the wombs of animals.
Those who are not freed from the bonds of Māra, nor from the realm of ghosts and the asuras,
yet remain intent upon day and night—
In the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
they extinguish the fire of passion,
constantly perceiving the foul.
But the supreme among men extinguish the fire of hatred with loving-kindness,
and the fire of delusion with wisdom.
Those wise ones, having extinguished that [craving] which leads to penetration,
remain untiring by day and night.
They attain final Nibbāna without remainder;
they have completely transcended suffering.
These seers of the Noble Truths are possessors of true knowledge.
The wise, through right knowledge,
having directly realized the destruction of birth,
do not come to further existence.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fourth.
